records.name: Montenegro
records.summary_text:
Montenegro is workable for trans visitors — the Western Balkans' most advanced legal framework. It has a same-sex partnership law (2020), anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and SOGI-inclusive hate-crime provisions; Podgorica Pride proceeds annually. Counterweights documented by ILGA-Europe: anti-LGBT and misogynistic hate speech in political rhetoric is a serious issue, and misdemeanour charges are overused in place of proper hate-crime prosecution (European Commission). There is no legal gender recognition law (administrative practice is inconsistent).

For a visitor: n

records.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
records.summary_text:
Bosnia and Herzegovina is workable for trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised; the capital Sarajevo’s Pride has proceeded annually since 2019 with heavy (necessary) police protection; and most cantons have now appointed prosecutors specifically for anti-LGBTI hate crimes — genuine institutional progress.

Counterweights from the 2024 Pink Report (the annual monitor): negative events are accumulating, the trend is unfavourable outside Sarajevo (especially in one internal region, Republika Srpska), and trans people occupy a “precarious position” — no legal gender recognition framework,
